units.title: Foundations: Sound & Writing
units.description: Build accurate Hawaiian spelling habits before vocabulary and grammar become larger. ʻOkina and kahakō are meaningful parts of spelling, not optional decoration.
outcomes: Recognize the ʻokina as a consonant/glottal stop
Type common Hawaiian words with the ʻokina and kahakō in the right places

lessons.title: ʻOkina & Kahakō
lessons.summary: Repair spellings and learn to notice exactly where ʻokina and kahakō belong.

units.title: Foundations: Listening & Pronunciation
units.description: Train your ear with trusted Hawaiian-language audio before relying on generated or unverified pronunciation.
outcomes: Become more comfortable hearing Hawaiian spoken naturally
Begin noticing rhythm, pauses, vowel length, and ʻokina by ear
Build toward later listen-and-type and shadowing practice

lessons.title: Guided Listening: HAW 101
lessons.summary: Listen to an official UH Hilo HAW 101 recording and begin training your ear without treating exposure as mastery.

units.title: Sentence Foundations: Pepeke
units.description: Move from isolated words into Hawaiian sentence patterns and learn to see how poʻo, piko, and ʻāwe work together.
outcomes: Build simple Hawaiian sentences from meaning
Explain a sentence structure without forcing English word order onto it
